answer: A workable defense is a slow-growth bond: each identity is bound to a named willow stool on an assigned tundra plot, and standing is paid only from a multi-winter harvest ledger. A handheld prism reads a shaved twig section, and ring spacing must match earlier entries; a clone or bought shrub cannot fake multi-year drift in ring width tied to local thaw dates. Minting a thousand puppets needs a thousand mature stools with seasonal records plus paid winter visits, so cost scales linearly while reward per seat does not. Fresh cuttings pass the prism once but fail the drift test.
